name: android-render-memory
description: Review set for the Android render and memory branch.

hillshade-cache.title: Hillshade preparation reuse and invalidation
hillshade-cache.focus:
This area caches the output of hillshade preparation across frames and is
enabled by default on Android. A reuse bug shows as a stale shaded relief that
survives an input change. Establish, for every input that feeds a prepared
hillshade output, whether a change to it reaches the cache key or an explicit
invalidation. Name any input that reaches neither. Check the retained geometry
path for ownership of buffers that the renderer may release independently,
and check what happens to retained outputs under a memory trim followed by a
new frame.

symbol-reuse.title: Symbol layer reuse and label update classification
symbol-reuse.focus:
Layer level symbol reuse is an opt in flag that skips rebuilding a symbol
layer when an update only moves labels. The risk is a skipped rebuild that
should not have been skipped, which drops or freezes text instead of making
the frame cheaper. Decide whether the position only classification is sound for
every field the layer reads, including text, icon, sort order, collision state
and per feature paint. Treat a missing field as a correctness defect, not a
style issue. Check that the diagnostics flag adds no work when it is off.

vertex-repack.title: Vertex repacking, staging storage and packed buffers
vertex-repack.focus:
These changes move vertex expansion into native code, pack line vertices more
tightly, copy extrusion paint attributes by word and reuse bounded staging
storage. Every one of them is a memory safety surface. For each entry point,
check that the destination capacity is derived from the same vertex count and
stride as the source, that a word sized copy cannot read or write past the end
of an odd sized span, and that a reused staging buffer cannot hand stale bytes
to a later frame with a different stride. State the exact input that triggers
any mismatch you find.

memory-pressure.title: Memory budgets, trimming and resource reclamation
memory-pressure.focus:
This area reclaims inactive buildings under pressure, preserves map images
while trimming, reports applied budgets and optionally accounts GPU buffers to
the garbage collector. Check the order between reclaiming a resource and the
next frame that may still reference it, and whether a trim can run while a
frame holds a reclaimed buffer. Check that a reported budget is the applied one
rather than the requested one on every path. Check that buffer accounting
cannot double count or fail to release its accounted size when a buffer dies on
an error path.

frame-lifecycle.title: Frame snapshots, async rendering and overlay callbacks
frame-lifecycle.focus:
Snapshots are released after frame preparation, asynchronous rendering is
enabled where the native side supports it and overlay callbacks now receive the
current frame. The risk is a use after release across the owner thread boundary
and a lost or duplicated frame publication. For each release point, establish
which thread owns the snapshot and whether any consumer can still read it.
Check that a frame published asynchronously cannot be adopted twice or dropped
while a camera update is in flight.

camera.title: Camera updates, relative zoom and native queries
camera.focus:
These changes avoid unnecessary native camera queries, fix relative zoom steps
and preserve frames during continuous camera updates. A cached camera value is
correct only while nothing else can move the camera. Establish what invalidates
the cached value and name any native side path that changes the camera without
going through it. Check that a relative zoom step composes correctly when
several updates queue up within one frame.

jni-cohosting.title: Android HTTP isolation and cohosted SDK symbols
jni-cohosting.focus:
The Android HTTP callback class moved to a package private to this plugin so
that it no longer collides with the MapLibre GL SDK when both are loaded. The
contract is that the Java class name and the name the native bridge registers
must match, and that neither side can be rebuilt alone. Check that every
reference agrees, including the consumer ProGuard rules and the test stubs.
Report any remaining symbol that both SDKs would still register, on Android or
on Darwin.

diagnostics-overhead.title: Diagnostics cost when the flags are off
diagnostics-overhead.focus:
Several commits add diagnostics and counters that ship disabled, alongside a
rewritten command export path. A diagnostic that costs work while disabled
quietly taxes every frame. For each counter and trace added on this branch,
state whether the disabled path still allocates, formats a string, reads a
clock or takes a lock. Also check that the faster command export path produces
the same decoded entries as the path it replaces, including for the cases the
new tests do not cover.

style.title: AGENTS.md comment and Dart style conformance
style.focus:
Check the whole branch diff against the repository AGENTS.md rules. The rules
that matter here are a blank line before a return that follows another
statement, no blank line when the preceding line closes a scope or the return
is alone in its scope, comments that document stable contracts rather than
history or tests, no em dashes, semicolons or label style colons in comment
prose, and no comment that only restates the code. Report each violation with
its file and line. Do not report anything outside the diff.
